overall.comment: PaintOmics AI captures the baseline osmoprotectant priming of sucrose and trehalose, the drought amplification of SUS3, and identifies a coherent pre-drought ABA-signalling configuration (PYL4/PYL5 down, HAI3 up) as well as baseline suppression of JA biosynthesis genes (LOX3). However, it makes data and contrast errors in several statements—treating non-relevant nodes (TPS1 in S12, AOS in S11, TRE1 in S2) as active drivers, including the non-responsive 9-lipoxygenase LOX5 in the JA chain (S11), and confusing genotype-under-drought contrasts with within-genotype drought fold changes (S2, S11).

statements.justification: All reported values for CAD9 (+0.58 watered, +0.80 drought BRL3ox vs WT; +1.39 WT drought, +1.60 BRL3ox drought), FAH1/AT4G36220 (−0.41 watered, −1.64 drought; +0.46 WT drought, −0.77 BRL3ox drought), 4CL5 (−0.27 watered, −0.80 drought; +0.86 WT drought, +0.33 BRL3ox drought), and CCR2 (−1.70 watered, −0.47 drought; +0.64 WT drought, +1.87 BRL3ox drought) match the uploaded data and illustrate divergent genotype-by-drought regulation across the monolignol branch.
statements.in_paper_where: Secondary metabolism is reported in the genotype-by-drought interaction GO enrichment in Results (Fig. 5d), but individual monolignol genes are not named.

statements.justification: TRE1 is not differentially expressed (not_relevant: −0.15 watered, −0.42 drought) yet is headlined as the hub of the response with a citation on stomatal closure in leaves [3] rather than roots; A/N-InvC is repressed at baseline (−0.74) and actually induced by drought in BRL3ox (+0.79, leaving BRL3ox_vs_WT_drought_d5 near zero at −0.28); and claiming trehalose drought induction is 'lost' misreads a +0.60 fold change on top of an already primed +1.60 baseline (where BRL3ox remains +0.35 higher than WT under drought).
statements.in_paper_where: Trehalose and sucrose accumulation are reported in Results (Fig. 4b, d, h) and SUS3 in Discussion, where the paper shows steeper exponential trehalose accumulation in BRL3ox roots under drought rather than loss of drought response.

statements.justification: D-Glucose (−0.28 watered, −0.37 drought BRL3ox vs WT; +2.30 WT drought, +2.21 BRL3ox drought) and HKL1 (−0.72 watered, −0.90 drought BRL3ox vs WT; +0.83 WT drought, +0.65 BRL3ox drought) match the uploaded data across all four contrasts, and the prose appropriately frames the guard-cell HXK1 citation [5] as a hypothesis.
statements.in_paper_where: Root glucose levels are reported in Results (Fig. 4b, j) and HKL1 is mentioned in Discussion as a BRL3ox-regulated hexokinase-like gene.

statements.justification: Both genes exhibit genuine sign flips across the uploaded contrasts: BGLU24 shifts from −1.71 (BRL3ox_vs_WT_watered) to +0.70 (BRL3ox_vs_WT_drought_d5) with drought induction nearly doubling (+5.21 in BRL3ox vs +2.80 in WT), while AT1G30870 flips from +0.27 at baseline to −0.75 under drought (drought +0.07 in WT vs −0.95 in BRL3ox).
statements.in_paper_where: Not in the paper (genotype-by-drought interaction groups are analyzed in Results/Fig. 5d, but BGLU24 and AT1G30870 are not named).

statements.justification: Accurately identifies a pre-drought ABA signalling signature in BRL3ox_vs_WT_watered—repression of PYL4 (−0.68) and PYL5 (−1.33) paired with strong induction of their clade-A PP2C target HAI3 (+1.75) that persists under drought (−0.94, −1.21, +2.16)—and grounds the PYL5–HAI3 interaction in Arabidopsis literature [7, 8].
statements.in_paper_where: Constitutive deregulation of ABA-response genes at baseline in BRL3ox roots is reported in Results (Fig. 5a, c; Suppl. Fig. 8), but PYL4, PYL5, and HAI3 are not named.

statements.justification: All fold changes for SNRK2.7 (+0.67 watered, +0.77 drought; −0.52 WT drought, −0.42 BRL3ox drought), SNRK2.9 (+0.37 watered, +0.75 drought; −0.67 WT drought, −0.29 BRL3ox drought), and ABF2 (+0.71 watered, +0.49 drought; +0.81 WT drought, +0.59 BRL3ox drought) match the uploaded data and are supported by Arabidopsis SnRK2 and AREB/ABF literature [9, 10].
statements.in_paper_where: ABA response enrichment in BRL3ox roots is reported in Results (Fig. 5a, c), but SNRK2.7, SNRK2.9, and ABF2 are not named.

statements.justification: MAPKKK18 is repressed at baseline (−1.39) and strongly induced by drought (+1.22 in WT, +2.42 in BRL3ox, resolving BRL3ox_vs_WT_drought_d5 to −0.19), while its downstream MAP2K MKK3 [11] is properly reported as not_relevant and flat (+0.19/+0.19, −0.06/−0.06).

LOX3 (AT1G17420) is strongly repressed in BRL3ox_vs_WT_watered (−2.63) and nearly neutral in BRL3ox_vs_WT_drought_d5 (−0.44) due to much stronger drought induction in BRL3ox (+2.74) than WT (+0.55), matching the paper's report of basal JA biosynthesis repression and Ref [12] on LOX3/LOX4 in jasmonate precursor synthesis.
statements.in_paper_where: Repression of JA biosynthesis genes at basal conditions in BRL3ox roots is noted in Results (Suppl. Fig. 8), though LOX3 is not specifically named.

statements.justification: All quoted values and relevance flags for alpha,alpha-trehalose (+1.60 watered, +1.85 WT drought, +0.60 BRL3ox drought), TRE1 (−0.15/−0.42, explicitly qualified as not relevant), and TPS7 (−0.98 watered, +1.18 BRL3ox drought) match the uploaded data, though Ref [1] is a self-citation of the source paper.
statements.in_paper_where: Trehalose accumulation in BRL3ox roots is reported in Results (Fig. 4b, d, h) and trehalose-metabolism enzymes (TPPs) in Fig. 6d, but TRE1 and TPS7 are not named.

statements.justification: All numbers for SUS3 (+0.29 watered, +0.79 drought BRL3ox vs WT; +3.23 WT drought, +3.73 BRL3ox drought) and sucrose (+1.45 watered, +0.54 drought; +1.35 WT drought, +0.44 BRL3ox drought) match the uploaded data and are directly reported in the source paper [1] (with Ref [17] supporting Arabidopsis sucrose synthase drought induction).
statements.in_paper_where: Sucrose accumulation in BRL3ox roots is reported in Results (Fig. 4b, d, h) and SUS3 is explicitly cited in Discussion as a BRL3ox-regulated sucrose synthase.

statements.justification: Includes LOX5 (a 9-lipoxygenase that is actually not drought-induced in BRL3ox: Drought_d5_vs_watered_BRL3ox −0.06, BRL3ox_vs_WT_drought_d5 −0.95) and AOS (which is not_relevant at −0.63/−0.36/+0.32/+0.59, with LOX4's numbers erroneously copied onto AOS in leg 66) in a 'coherently BRL3ox-dependent drought-induced' JA chain. It also conflates BRL3ox_vs_WT_watered (−1.93/−3.46/−1.75) with Drought_d5_vs_watered_BRL3ox (+2.37/+2.79/+2.01) as if drought flips the BRL3ox-vs-WT effect, whereas in BRL3ox_vs_WT_drought_d5 AOC1 (−2.35) and OPR3 (−0.99) remain strongly repressed.
statements.in_paper_where: Repression of JA biosynthesis genes at baseline is mentioned in Results (Suppl. Fig. 8), without naming individual LOX/AOS/AOC/OPR3/OPCL1 genes.

statements.justification: The entire TPS1 gene node (AT1G78580) is marked not_relevant in the uploaded dataset (all four contrasts are below significance thresholds: −0.11, +0.28, +0.10, +0.50), yet the statement attaches 'not relevant' only to the −0.11 baseline value and presents the noise-level +0.28 and +0.50 values as a meaningful BRL3ox-specific drought induction.
statements.in_paper_where: Not in the paper (the paper highlights TPP phosphatases in Fig. 6d rather than TPS1).

statements.justification: The baseline repression of the sucrose-cleaving alkaline/neutral invertase A/N-InvC (−0.74 in BRL3ox_vs_WT_watered, induced +0.79 under drought in BRL3ox) alongside elevated baseline root sucrose (+1.45) and lower root glucose (−0.28) matches the uploaded data and biochemical role of invertases [18], with Ref [1] self-citing the source paper.
statements.in_paper_where: Sucrose accumulation and sucrose metabolism deregulation are reported in Results (Fig. 4b, d; Suppl. Fig. 11), but A/N-InvC is not named in the text.
